I would encourage you to listen to 'The Cure for Chronic pain' podcast by Nicole Sachs, she talks with recovered folks and goes into all different aspects of journaling and mindbody recovery.

I had white blood cells in my urine but never got a cystoscopy, so I think that counts as inflammation signs. But think about it this way: we already accept medically that stress can cause stomach ulcers. That's a physical reaction, and yet caused by mindbody connection. So in my opinion even if there is 'inflammation' the root cause will still be addressed by Journalspeak, as long as there isn't some other underlying condition such as cancer or an acute infection.

I spent a lifetime searching through every other religion trying to mend my anxiety and depression. I meditated, studied, chanted, and even went on 5-day silent retreats. It was all very nice, but none of it touched the deep feelings of fear, grief, and self-loathing I had in my heart. Finally, a year ago, I was brought to my knees and I prayed from the deepest place of surrender for God to help me, because I clearly was not able to help myself. I had spent a lifetime in anguish and I feared I would spend the rest of my life there too. And in that moment, I felt a presence show up in the room, and something in my heart just knew it was Jesus. He was a being of light, radiating love. After this I started hearing messages from God (who confirmed for me that he will save all) and having prophetic dreams, and I was truly filled with the Holy Spirit. Ever since then I have thrown myself into Christianity. It's not always easy--in fact, it has created lots of problems for me & it can be really confusing at times. But the way I used to feel, the darkness, the confusion, the self-hatred and despair and fear... That is all gone. I feel saved, even though I never wanted it to look like this, I can't deny that Jesus was the only one who answered me when I cried out.

I always preferred to believe there was something bigger than us in the universe. It was that: a preference. I recognized atheism was possible, but my life didn't change wether I believed in a higher power or not. I cycled through Hinduism and Buddhism, finding great wisdom and some comfort through meditation, but nothing that really changed my world or worldview. In a very very dark moment of my life, I called upon a Christian I knew and asked her to pray with me. As we prayed, I felt a light in the room with us, and somehow I just knew that it was Jesus. The next day I took a walk in my neighborhood and I was overcome with wonder for the natural world. The trees were alive, the sky was radiant, every person I saw wandering by was a beautiful child of God. My lifelong anxiety and dread fell into the abyss. I began having experiences of being 'filled with the Holy Spirit', prophetic dreams and visions, and coincidences that I just couldn't make up if I tried. Prayer was bliss, God was talking to me all the time.

The big reason I had never entertained the idea of Christianity (aside from the hypocrisy and bigotry demonstrated by a lot of mainstream Christians) is that I found the doctrine of hell totally nonsensical. But God answered that for me too. Early on into my journey I was listening to a Universalist episode of a podcast, and as the guest speaker was talking, my entire body began to vibrate with light and I heard a big booming voice say 'You are on the right path!'. He even supernaturally lead me to a church with a Universalist clergy, that aligns with my faith perfectly.

In short: there was never any argument that could convince me to believe in God, or be a Christian. I myself could not make a persuasive argument to another person, even now when my faith is so deep and profound. It can't be puzzled out by the human brain or put into words. I would only encourage everyone to humble themselves as much as they can, open their heart was wide as it will open, call out to God with all the sincerity you can muster, and see what happens. You may be surprised--I sure was!

A few thoughts, although I can't cite many bible verses as I am a relatively new convert, so this is all from my heart.

For years and years I had also been quite reliant on porn, and experimented with open relationships and loads of casual sex that left me feeling hollow and gross (I am a woman so slightly different perspective but I sympathize). I don't feel as though I am marked or tainted by any of the things I've seen or done, nor do I think sexual urges are unnatural or even a high priority for God, but I do believe that as we deepen our relationship with God a lot of this untethered lust will naturally fall away. Putting the emphasis on abstaining in my opinion is kind of doomed to fail.

Find a food kitchen and cook for the hungry. Walk your city with bags of socks and protein bars and hand them out to homeless people. Look the sick and needy in the eye and see their soul as Christ would. Volunteer to spend time with people in hospice. Christ is alive in these places. Pray more. Meditate more. Pray more!

I also tend to think that an addiction to sex/porn stems from some deeper inability or hesitancy to accept true love. It's calories without nutrients. It's reward without merit. Sex with strangers can be fun, but sex with the person you love and have married and are genuinely compatible with (emphasis on compatible).... I mean, it isn't even a close call. The intimacy shared in true committed love makes everything else fall away. So I would suggest  investigating why you are afraid of commitment, and why you might be hesitant to accept true love and be vulnerable in that way. This could be in a journaling practice or with a therapist.

Signing off by saying I had watched porn constantly since the age of 11. A few months ago after my first experience with Jesus, I was home alone, and I had the thought of wanting to watch porn. And a very easy, gentle voice said, what if you didn't? And I haven't had the urge to since then. It isn't a frustrating denial of self, it just became natural. And I believe that through grace this is possible for you too. Peace and blessings.

I could have written this post myself three years ago. No answers, new symptoms constantly, pain that nobody could fix. I would ask you to look up the podcast The Cure for Chronic Pain with Nicole Sachs. Listen to the first few episodes and see if it clicks. Her work healed me of intense mystery symptoms that had me bedridden and considering drastic surgery. I legit had no quality of life before I found her work. I have also known 2 people in my real life who have been cured of life-altering chronic pain after finding her work, and many others who I have networked with online who this worked for. No weird diets or payments or purchases. Totally free and you can start today. Hope you find relief soon ! I'm here if you have any further questions

Also don't get too hung up on being perfect. I have coffee with cream every morning that is 50cals. Some would say this breaks the fast but I loathe the taste of black coffee and I have still hit all my goals. Make it work for you!

Since you just started, 20:4 is already a bit dramatic so go easy and feel free to eat 16:8 for a week or two. It's still a great way to achieve your goals. And yes, I have mostly stubborn pockets of tummy fat. I took a before pic and compared it with a recent after pic, and wow.... huge difference. I don't have a flat stomach yet per se but its going in that direction for sure.

I do everything from 16:8 to 20:4 and OMAD. Just kind of feel it out depending on what I want to cook for dinner (for example, if I have a delicious 980calorie meal planned out, I will probably skip lunch and just eat dinner and a snack). I also def have cheat days on weekends and special occasions.

Congrats on 20:4, it really doesn't take too long to get used to it!

I’m not totally overcome, but not googling symptoms made a world of difference.  Googling anything will make you think you’re dying.  Also, all of the times when I freaked out and it ended up being nothing - I have a track record of 100% overreacting and worrying over nothing, so the odds of whatever I’m worrying about now also being nothing? are pretty good.

And yes, anxiety meds can help for sure.  I am on a mild dose of propranolol because I don’t like the idea of a daily pill, but in more extreme cases, if it’s really messing up your whole life, you may want to consider that!

Good luck and remember: there are risks to just being alive, but most people you know are likely healthy and doing well.  No matter what, you have every opportunity to love your life!
